standard.title: Initiate and sustain exchanges about experiences and views
standard.description: initiate and sustain exchanges in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts related to students' experiences, feelings and views, adjusting their language in response to others
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can initiate and sustain modelled exchanges in familiar contexts expressing feelings, opinions and preferences (AC9LS6C01). They have not yet initiated exchanges in unfamiliar contexts, structured arguments, or adjusted language in real time in response to others.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students initiate and sustain exchanges in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts about experiences, feelings and views — including structuring arguments, inviting opinions, and adjusting language in response to others.

nodes.label: Exchanging experiences and structuring arguments
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can exchange accounts of experiences and use structured language to justify positions and invite others' opinions.
nodes.minimum_width: Share at least one account of a past experience using sequenced language; use at least one argument-structuring expression; invite at least one opinion from a partner.
nodes.typical_width: Develop narrative skills by exchanging significant events and milestones; use structured argument language to justify positions; invite others' opinions; use open-ended questions and connectors to initiate and extend conversations; interact with target language community peers about shared interests.
wider: Exchange a substantive account of a significant experience — providing context, sequence of events and personal reaction beyond a simple summary
Argue a position using at least three argument-structuring moves — assertion, reason and acknowledgement of a counterposition
nodes.hinge_reason: Justifying positions and inviting opinions are the interactional moves that distinguish exchange from conversation. They are required for the collaborative and analytical tasks at this band. Students who can only share information without arguing or inviting dialogue cannot reach these demands.

response_modes.reason: Argument-structuring expressions and opinion-invitation formulae need to become automatic across varied topics before they are available spontaneously in interaction.

success_criteria: Shares at least one account of a past experience using sequenced language
Uses at least one argument-structuring expression and invites a partner's opinion during an exchange

nodes.label: Adjusting language across contexts and registers
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can adjust their language in response to others and across different contexts — using appropriate register for formal and informal interactions.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate register adjustment in at least two different interaction contexts; make at least one real-time adjustment in response to a partner's contribution.
nodes.typical_width: Use appropriate register across formal and informal contexts; adjust language in response to others' contributions; use formal and informal address appropriately for varied interlocutors; sustain exchanges in some unfamiliar contexts using available strategies.
wider: Participate in an interaction that shifts register mid-exchange — demonstrate real-time adjustment without prompting
Record and review a sustained exchange — identify every instance where register was or should have been adjusted and explain the social signal that triggered each

response_modes.reason: Register adjustment develops through encountering varied interaction contexts. Single-register practice does not build the adjustment capacity that authentic interaction demands.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Real-time register adjustment distinguishes advanced from intermediate speakers. Width investment here produces qualitatively different interactional capacity.
success_criteria: Uses appropriate register in at least two different interaction contexts
Makes at least one identifiable language adjustment during an exchange in response to a partner's contribution or contextual shift
